title: Timers in Function Block Diagram: an off-delay light and an on-delay filter
summary: Connect a TOF block to keep a light on after a push button is released, and a TON block to ignore a sensor blip that is too short.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real push button bounces or how fast a real sensor answers.
objectives: Keep an output ON for a fixed time after its input drops, with a timer block whose PT input is wired to a TIME constant.
Ignore an input that is ON for less than a fixed time, and say which timer delays the start and which one delays the end.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Delays.fbd.json Button is connected straight to Light and Sensor straight to Confirmed. Make Light stay ON for {{t:300}} ms after Button is released, and make Confirmed turn ON only after Sensor has stayed ON for {{t:200}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which timer block keeps an output on and which one waits before turning it on.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The scenario presses Button at {{t:100}} ms and releases it at {{t:300}} ms. Sensor blips ON from {{t:100}} ms to {{t:140}} ms and is ON again from {{t:500}} ms to {{t:900}} ms. Predict Light and Confirmed at {{t:200}}, {{t:450}}, {{t:650}}, and {{t:800}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:Delays.Light=true,Delays.Confirmed=false@200|Light ON, Confirmed OFF}} at {{t:200}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=true,Delays.Confirmed=false@450|Light ON, Confirmed OFF}} at {{t:450}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=false,Delays.Confirmed=false@650|both OFF}} at {{t:650}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=false,Delays.Confirmed=true@800|Confirmed ON, Light OFF}} at {{t:800}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting diagram, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting diagram connects the inputs straight to the outputs, so Light is already OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed turns ON with the short blip at {{t:100}} ms. Change it so that Light stays ON until {{t:300}} ms after Button is released, and Confirmed turns ON only when Sensor has been ON for {{t:200}} ms without a break. Choose and place the blocks yourself.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named Delays and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Follow Light and Confirmed in the trace: the short blip never turns Confirmed ON, Light is still ON at {{t:450}} ms although Button went OFF at {{t:300}} ms, and Confirmed rises about {{t:200}} ms after Sensor came back at {{t:500}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: Light falls about {{t:300}} ms after Button, and Confirmed rises about {{t:200}} ms after the second Sensor pulse.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Think about what each timer answers: which one tells you how long a signal has been on, and which one tells you how long ago it went off? Then imagine a timer whose PT nothing reaches: what would your output do with the short blip at {{t:100}} ms?
stages.checkpoint: One timer delays the start of a signal and the other delays its end; each answers a different question. With nothing on PT the preset is zero, so the output would follow its input and turn ON with the short blip.

hints.text: Look at the two connections that run straight from an input to an output. For each output, ask whether its delay belongs to the start of its input or to its end.

Place a TOF block named HoldTimer with Button connected to IN and a TIME constant T#300ms to PT, and connect its Q to Light. Place a TON block named FilterTimer with Sensor on IN and a TIME constant T#200ms on PT, and connect its Q to Confirmed. Remove the two connections from the inputs straight to the outputs.

faultCases: The starting diagram connects the inputs straight to the outputs, so Light is already OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed turns ON with the short blip at {{t:100}} ms.
